Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Acute worsening of widespread pruritic, erythematous, dry, cracked dermatitis predominantly in flexural areas; known atopic eczema and asthma; no systemic symptoms; OTC hydrocortisone and prior OTC antihistamine ineffective; using emollients and wash product consistently; no signs of weeping or exudate reported.
- DDx (consistent with transcript and DDx model):  
  - Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare is most consistent.  
  - Consider superimposed allergic/irritant contact dermatitis given distribution on hands/arms/chest despite unchanged products.  
  - Monitor for secondary bacterial infection given skin cracks, although no current signs (no weeping/crusting/fever).
- Working diagnosis: Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare.
- Plan:  
  - Prescribed fexofenadine (dose not documented).  
  - Prescribed Betnovate (betamethasone valerate) topical twice daily for 2 weeks with fingertip unit guidance.  
  - Continue emollients and soap substitute.  
  - Safety net: return sooner if worsening; otherwise reassess in ~2 weeks; seek care for any adverse reactions.  
  - Pharmacy: prescription sent to Boots (per clinician).
- Conflicts noted: Family history—patient reports maternal hypothyroidism; clinician repeated “hyperthyroidism.”

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare — High likelihood: Classic flexural, pruritic, dry, erythematous rash with patient history of eczema and atopic comorbidity (asthma), acute worsening over days.  
- Allergic or irritant contact dermatitis — Medium likelihood: Distribution on hands/arms/chest could reflect exposure-related dermatitis superimposed on atopic skin despite no reported product changes.  
- Secondary bacterial infection (impetiginized eczema) — Low–Medium likelihood: Cracked skin increases risk, but absence of weeping/crusting/fever lowers current probability.
